passage:
First year in the hostel, I was so lonely I could hear my own heartbeat at night. Then I met Rehana in the mess queue. By day three I'd bought her earrings. By day five I was messaging her forty times a day and calling her my soul sister. I planned a holiday trip for us without asking her.
She started taking longer to reply. When she went to dinner with her roommates, I sent a long message about how hurt I was. She said, very gently, "Manjula, this is a lot, really fast."
I was furious at first. Now I see it. I wasn't building a friendship; I was trying to lock one in before it could leave. The counsellor I saw that term said the speed was the warning sign. We're friends now, slowly. Properly.

qa.q: What had Manjula bought Rehana by day three?
qa.a: Manjula had bought her earrings.

qa.q: What feeling was driving Manjula's rush to get close?
qa.a: Loneliness; Manjula was so lonely at night and wanted to lock the friendship in before it could leave.

qa.q: What turning point helped Manjula change?
qa.a: Rehana's gentle "this is a lot, really fast" and seeing a counsellor helped Manjula recognise the speed as the warning sign and slow down.

qa.q: What was it like for Rehana to receive forty messages a day?
qa.a: She probably felt overwhelmed and pressured, which is why she took longer to reply and named it gently.

grounding: A young adult recalls flooding a new friend with gifts, messages and plans within days out of loneliness, and learns that the intensity was the warning sign.

passage:
I've known Ujjwal since school, so I noticed when he met Tanya at the college fest. Within a week he was sending flowers to her hostel every day, posting that she was "the one", and talking about moving cities for her. He wanted her with him every evening and sulked when she went to her cousin's birthday instead.
I can't see inside his head. He's been lonely since his parents moved abroad, and maybe it's only that. But the speed scared me, and so did the sulking.
I told him, "This is very fast, and it's okay for her to have her own plans." He laughed. "Ganga, you worry too much." Two days later Tanya told me she felt smothered and didn't know how to say it. I said she didn't have to decide anything quickly, and she could talk to the college counsellor or me any time.

qa.q: What did Ujjwal send to Tanya's hostel?
qa.a: He was sending flowers to her hostel every day.

qa.q: What does Ganga think might be behind Ujjwal's intensity?
qa.a: Ganga thinks it may be loneliness since his parents moved abroad, though Ganga can't be sure, and the sulking is worrying too.

qa.q: What did Ganga tell Tanya that was a wise step?
qa.a: Ganga said Tanya didn't have to decide anything quickly and could talk to the college counsellor or Ganga any time.

qa.q: How might Ujjwal feel if Tanya asks for more space?
qa.a: He might feel hurt and afraid of being left alone, given his loneliness, which could show up as more sulking.

grounding: An old schoolmate watches a young man flood a new partner with attention and big promises within days, and sees the intensity itself as the warning sign.

passage:
In the first-year girls' hostel, Mahima had known Lakshmi for exactly six days.
On day two, Mahima bought her a scarf. On day three, a card: "Best friends forever. I've never met anyone like you." On day four, she moved her mattress into Lakshmi's room "for company." On day five, she cried when Lakshmi went to the library with other girls. By day six, she'd sent forty-three messages.
That night, Lakshmi sat on her bed. "Mahima, I like you. But this is too much, too fast. I need some space."
Mahima felt the floor drop. She went back to her own room and sat in the dark. She'd never lived away from home. Every quiet evening in the hostel felt like falling. Lakshmi had been something to hold.
The next morning, she walked to the hostel counsellor's office and knocked. "I think I'm scaring people away," she said. "Because I'm scared of being alone."

qa.q: How many messages had Mahima sent by day six?
qa.a: She'd sent forty-three messages.

qa.q: What was Mahima feeling when Lakshmi asked for space?
qa.a: Mahima felt crushed and panicked, as if the floor dropped, because she was deeply lonely away from home.

qa.q: What wise step did Mahima take?
qa.a: She went to the hostel counsellor and named what was happening, that her fear of being alone was making her overwhelm people.

qa.q: How did Lakshmi experience the first six days?
qa.a: Lakshmi felt overwhelmed and uneasy, liking Mahima but finding the gifts, messages and crying too much, too fast.

grounding: It shows a lonely young adult flooding a new friend with gifts, messages and promises of forever within days, and the intensity being the warning sign.

passage:
Dear Yusuf Bhai,
You asked what happened with Neha. I'll tell you properly, because I think I need to hear it myself.
I met her at the college fest. By the fourth day I'd bought her flowers, a bracelet and a concert ticket. I told her I'd never felt this way, that we were meant to be. I messaged her from waking up till I slept. When she went out with her cousins, I called seven times.
I told myself it was love. But it wasn't only love. I wanted to lock it in before she could change her mind. Before she could see the boring, lonely parts of me.
On day nine she said, "You're amazing, but this scares me," and ended it.
I was angry for a week. Now I think she was right. If someone did that to me, I'd be scared too.
I've started seeing the college counsellor. Can we talk on Sunday?
Chinmay

qa.q: How many times did Chinmay call when Neha went out with her cousins?
qa.a: He called seven times.

qa.q: What was Chinmay feeling underneath the gifts and messages?
qa.a: Chinmay felt lonely and afraid of being seen as boring, and he wanted to lock the relationship in before she could change her mind.

qa.q: What step is Chinmay taking now?
qa.a: Chinmay has started seeing the college counsellor and is reaching out to Yusuf to talk on Sunday.

qa.q: How did Neha experience those nine days?
qa.a: Neha felt scared and overwhelmed by the intensity, even though she thought Chinmay was amazing.

grounding: A young adult writes to Yusuf Bhai about flooding a new partner with gifts, calls and promises within days, and seeing the intensity as the warning sign.

passage:
Can I just talk, Gopika, without you taking notes? Okay. You can take notes.
So. I met Rohan at the library on a Monday. By Wednesday, I'd made him a playlist, a card and cookies. By Friday I'd said, "I've never connected with anyone like this." By Sunday I was planning his birthday, which is in November. I sent him good-morning and good-night messages. Voice notes. Photos of everything.
On Tuesday he said, "Arohi, you're sweet, but I barely know you."
I was so angry. How could he not see how much I cared?
But you asked me last week what I was afraid of. And I think… it's being forgotten. Everyone in my family is busy. If I give someone everything, fast, they can't leave. That's the idea, right? Except it made him want to leave.
I don't want to do that again. What do I do instead?

qa.q: On which day did Rohan say he barely knew Arohi?
qa.a: On Tuesday.

qa.q: What does Arohi say she is afraid of?
qa.a: Arohi says she is afraid of being forgotten, which made her rush to give someone everything so they could not leave.

qa.q: What could Gopika help Arohi try next time?
qa.a: Gopika could help Arohi slow down, let a friendship or relationship grow at a normal pace, and find other support for the loneliness.

qa.q: How did Rohan experience that first week?
qa.a: Rohan felt overwhelmed and uneasy at the flood of gifts, messages and plans from someone he barely knew.

grounding: A young adult tells a counsellor about overwhelming a new partner with affection within days out of fear of being forgotten, and wanting to change.

passage:
Day 2: Charu had met Pranav at the college film club only on Saturday, but by Monday she had sent him forty messages, a playlist titled "Us", and a photo of two train tickets to Shimla "for our first trip". Her new hostel room was so quiet at night; his replies made it feel full.
Day 5: She turned up at his lab with lunch, a handmade card and a promise: "I've never felt this with anyone. We're forever." Pranav laughed awkwardly and said he had a group project. Charu's stomach dropped. She texted him eleven times that evening.
Day 12: Pranav asked to slow down. Charu cried, then called her school friend Leena, who asked gently, "Do you even know his favourite food?" Charu didn't. She sat with that for a long time, and admitted how lonely her first weeks in the city had been.

qa.q: What was the playlist Charu sent called?
qa.a: The playlist was titled Us.

qa.q: Why did Charu keep flooding Pranav with messages?
qa.a: Charu felt lonely in her quiet new hostel room, and Pranav's replies made it feel full, so she clung anxiously to the new bond.

qa.q: What small step could help Charu the next time she feels a rush like this?
qa.a: She could let a new bond grow at a normal pace, keep leaning on friends like Leena, and treat the speed itself as a sign she is racing ahead of knowing the person.

qa.q: What is it like for Pranav to hear promises of forever within a week?
qa.a: Pranav seems uncomfortable and overwhelmed; he laughs awkwardly, points to his project, and finally asks to slow down.

grounding: Shows a lonely young adult flooding a new acquaintance with messages, plans and promises of forever within days, where the speed is the warning sign.
